When N ≤ T 1−ǫ we may evaluate M1 (R, T ) and M2 (R, T ) easily. These are two quadratic
forms in the unknown coefficients r(n), and the problem thus reduces to maximizing the
ratio of these quadratic forms. Solving this optimization problem we obtain Theorem 1.
   This method generalizes readily to provide large and small central values in families of
L-functions. By contrast, the method of Montgomery does not appear to generalize to this
situation. Recently Z. Rudnick and the author ([11] and [12]) found a flexible method to
obtain lower bounds for moments in many families of L-functions, but the bounds obtained
here are superior.

section_entries.mathematical_role: Uses harmonic weights, Petersson's trace formula, a central approximate functional equation, and Hecke relations to transfer the resonator to a cusp-form family.

unit_result_entry.unit_type: prime-sign selection in an automorphic family
unit_result_entry.why_material: Rankin factorization of the unweighted and central-value quadratic forms produces a positive prime cross term for f and its sign reversal for mu f, completing the family transfer of the resonance mechanism.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Hecke multiplication and Petersson orthogonality turn the weighted central moment into a gcd kernel
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Expanding the resonator and approximate functional equation, using Hecke relations, and applying the trace formula collapses the family average to a quadratic form with sigma(gcd(m,n))/sqrt(mn), with the smooth weight replaced by one under controlled errors.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Concentrating a multiplicative resonator on a calibrated prime window makes the favorable cross terms factor locally, and repeated Rankin bounds show that finite length does not destroy the Euler-product gain.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The tuning depends on each averaging error and cannot be extended to arbitrarily long resonators from these arguments.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Sparse prime support creates coherence while Rankin's trick licenses finite truncation

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Using f aligns prime contributions and makes the weighted ratio large, while multiplying by Möbius reverses the cross terms and makes it small, in both quadratic-character and cusp-form families.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The existence inference relies on each family's weighted-average setup and does not assert that every central value is positive or nonzero.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Prime-level sign modulation selects which extreme the same family average detects

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Once both cusp-form moments factor locally, the same prime sign switch used for quadratic characters again chooses constructive or destructive central-value alignment.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: With N=k/100 and r=f, Rankin's trick makes the unweighted moment asymptotic to product_p(1+f(p)^2), while the central moment has local factors containing a positive cross term. Taking r=mu f reverses that term and supplies the small-value conclusion.
directed.conceptual_reading: The transferable part of resonance is not a particular orthogonality formula but a modular architecture: obtain a diagonal family average, expose local cross terms, and choose their signs.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Euler products bridge the gcd-kernel quadratic form to prime-local rewards, making the f versus mu f comparison transparent.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The argument proves existence within the harmonically weighted family and does not identify a specific cusp form; its asymptotic scale depends on prior length and trace estimates.
directed.uncertainty: The local factors, constants, and final exponential scale are formula-sensitive and should be checked in the PDF.

inference: Prime-local sign control is a reasonable reading of the f versus mu f choice.
unsupported_or_imported: The claim that this is the same switch used for quadratic characters and the modular architecture involving other averaging laws imports material from other units; this span itself only completes the cusp-form case.
